policies.title: PM Awas Yojana — Urban Housing Scheme
policies.summary: Subsidised home loans for first-time urban homebuyers from low- and middle-income groups.
policies.eligibility: First-time homebuyers in EWS/LIG/MIG income brackets, urban households without a pucca house.

roadmap.detail: Confirm your income bracket and that your household doesn't already own a pucca house.
Submit via the PMAY-U portal or your nearest Common Service Centre with income and ID proof.
Your Urban Local Body and lending bank verify documents and, often, the site — typically 4–6 weeks.
The interest subsidy is credited directly to your home loan account.

policies.title: Municipal Solid Waste Grievance Redressal
policies.summary: The timeline SLAs your municipal corporation is legally bound to for garbage-collection complaints.
policies.eligibility: Any resident within municipal corporation limits — no application needed, the SLA applies automatically.

roadmap.detail: Your report is timestamped the moment it reaches the ward office.
The ward is required to acknowledge and schedule a collection run within 24 hours.
Backlog clearance is mandated within 3 working days of the complaint.
Wards missing the SLA three times in a quarter are flagged for corporation-level review.

policies.title: Jal Jeevan Mission — Piped Water Supply
policies.summary: Guarantees functional household tap water; leaks and outages have a mandated repair window under the mission.
policies.eligibility: All households, with priority for areas lacking a functional household tap connection.

roadmap.detail: Logged against the local Public Health Engineering division.
A field engineer assesses the leak or supply gap, usually within 48 hours.
Pipeline repair or new household connection is carried out under the mission's funded works.
Restoration is logged against the village/ward's functional household tap connection count.

policies.title: PMGSY — Road Maintenance & Pothole SLA
policies.summary: Defines how fast PWD must respond to potholes and road-safety hazards on notified roads.
policies.eligibility: Applies to any PWD-notified road; report the exact stretch and nearest landmark for fastest routing.

roadmap.detail: Location and severity logged against the nearest PWD division.
Injury-risk and repeat-mention signals decide priority — accident-linked reports jump the queue.
Field inspection and patching work, typically within 5 working days for high-priority reports.
A follow-up inspection closes the case only once the patch has held through the next rain.

policies.title: Saubhagya — Electrical Safety & Connections
policies.summary: Covers free/subsidised household electrification and safety response for exposed wiring or transformer faults.
policies.eligibility: All households for safety response; free connections prioritised for below-poverty-line households.

roadmap.detail: Sparking, exposed wiring, or outage logged against the local Electricity Board division.
Fire/shock-risk keywords fast-track a field engineer dispatch, often same-day.
Faulty equipment is repaired or replaced and the line is re-certified safe.
Eligible households without a connection are enrolled for free electrification under the scheme.

policies.title: Smart Street Lighting Maintenance Scheme
policies.summary: Ward-level SLA for streetlight repair, prioritised by pedestrian-safety and crime-report proximity.
policies.eligibility: Any public street within municipal limits.

roadmap.detail: Pole number and stretch logged against the Ward Office.
Nearby reports are merged into one work order so a whole dark stretch is fixed in one visit.
Routine maintenance visits typically close these within 48 hours.
